data.name: Pollo a la Crema With Poblano Strips
data.description: Tender chicken strips simmer with sweet onion and earthy poblano pepper in a silky Mexican crema sauce. Gentle chile warmth and tangy cream make this a comforting dinner ready in 30 minutes.

refrigerator.notes: Refrigerate in shallow, covered containers within 2 hours of cooking, or within 1 hour when the ambient temperature exceeds 32°C (90°F). Keep at 4°C (40°F) or below. Cooked poultry generally keeps for 3–4 days; this recipe uses a 3-day limit. [FoodSafety.gov storage guidance](https://www.foodsafety.gov/food-safety-charts/cold-food-storage-charts).

freezer.notes: Freeze cooled portions in airtight containers at -18°C (0°F) or below. The cream sauce may separate after thawing. Thaw overnight in the refrigerator.

storage.reheating: Warm gently in a saucepan over low heat, stirring frequently, until the chicken and sauce reach 74°C (165°F). Avoid a vigorous boil.

items.name: chicken breast
items.notes: Weigh the edible meat after removing any bones, skin and tough tendons. Cut into strips as directed; serve all the chicken with the sauce.

items.name: salt
items.notes: A moderate starting amount because Mexican crema varies in saltiness.

items.name: white onion
items.notes: Edible weight after removing the papery skin and root end.

items.name: poblano pepper
items.notes: Edible weight after removing stems, seeds and pale inner ribs; leave the green skin on.

items.name: mexican crema
items.notes: Use plain Mexican crema made with pasteurized dairy.

items.name: water
items.notes: For thinning the crema into a sauce; the liquid stays in the dish.

instructions.text: Slice the prepared onion and poblano into strips approximately 3 mm thick on the vegetable cutting board.
Slice the chicken across the grain into strips approximately 1 cm thick on the separate raw-poultry cutting board.
tips: Do not rinse raw chicken. Wash hands with soap after handling it, and wash and sanitize the knife, poultry board and contaminated surfaces before they touch cooked food.

instructions.text: Season the chicken in the mixing bowl with the salt, garlic powder and black pepper, distributing the seasonings evenly.
Heat the olive oil in the deep skillet over medium heat until it flows freely and shimmers lightly.
Sauté the onion and poblano in the oil for 7 minutes, stirring regularly with the cooking spoon, until softened with a few golden edges.

doneness_cues.visual: The onion is translucent and the poblano strips bend easily.

instructions.text: Sauté the seasoned chicken with the vegetables for 4 minutes over medium-high heat, stirring to separate the strips. The chicken will finish cooking in the sauce.

doneness_cues.visual: The chicken surfaces turn opaque; this is not the final safety check.

instructions.text: Stir the Mexican crema and water into the chicken and vegetables over low heat until the sauce is evenly combined.

doneness_cues.visual: A smooth, pale sauce surrounds the chicken and vegetables.

instructions.text: Simmer gently for about 5 minutes, until the thickest chicken strips reach an internal temperature of 74°C (165°F), checked with the instant-read thermometer. Maintain only small bubbles around the edges; continue cooking if the chicken has not reached the safe temperature.

doneness_cues.visual: The sauce lightly coats the chicken and shows small bubbles rather than a rolling boil.

instructions.text: Divide all the chicken, vegetables and sauce among four serving plates.

troubleshooting.symptom: The cream sauce looks grainy or oily.
troubleshooting.likely_cause: The crema boiled vigorously or was heated too quickly.
troubleshooting.prevention: Lower the heat before adding the crema and maintain a gentle simmer.
troubleshooting.fix: Remove the skillet from the heat briefly and stir gently until the sauce comes together as much as possible. If the chicken is below 74°C (165°F), resume gentle cooking until it reaches that temperature. A severely split sauce may remain grainy.

troubleshooting.likely_cause: Uneven strips caused smaller pieces to overcook while thicker pieces finished.
troubleshooting.prevention: Cut consistent 1 cm strips and check their internal temperature promptly.
troubleshooting.fix: Coat the chicken generously with the sauce and serve immediately. Lost moisture cannot be fully restored.

chef_notes: Thinly sliced fresh poblano softens quickly enough for this preparation without a separate roasting and peeling stage.
Full-fat Mexican crema gives the sauce body and a gentle tang; a rolling boil can damage its smooth texture.
Slice chicken across the grain for shorter muscle fibers and a more tender bite.

Use the thermometer reading, rather than color alone, to confirm doneness. Poultry and reheated leftovers must reach 74°C (165°F). [FoodSafety.gov temperature guidance](https://www.foodsafety.gov/food-safety-charts/safe-minimum-internal-temperatures).
data.cultural_context: Pollo con crema is a Mexican chicken preparation with a creamy sauce, and poblano and onion are familiar additions. Mexican crema contributes the characteristic richness and light tang. [Pollo con crema background](https://www.holajalapeno.com/pollo-con-crema-recipes/).
